analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction about a £650 payment made by bank transfer to a fraudster and alleges financial loss (CH-1). The payment was made by the customer and not via a bank error, so the case is a complaint.
analysis.summary: Customer paid a £650 deposit by bank transfer on 27/10/2026 for a used car found on an online marketplace. The seller had sent photos and a fake logbook, communicated over WhatsApp, and blocked the customer after payment. The customer reported it by phone on 30/10/2026 and emailed WhatsApp screenshots. She says she did not share bank security details. She wants her money back. This is a suspected authorised push payment scam and must go to Fraud & Scams within 1 business day (FRD-2). No vulnerability indicators were found and the customer was asked. The account protection check, payee details and the sending account are not recorded in the file. The bank must not promise reimbursement before the specialist decision (FRD-5).

timeline.event: Customer paid £650 deposit by bank transfer to a seller met on an online marketplace for a used car
Seller sent photos and a fake logbook and communicated via WhatsApp
After payment, the seller blocked the customer
Customer reported the matter by phone; did not share bank security details; no vulnerability identified and customer was asked; WhatsApp screenshots emailed in

analysis.severity_reason: Suspected scam under CH-6 (High). Financial loss of £650 alone would be Medium.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None identified. Confirm preferred contact method at handover.

analysis.routing_reason: Suspected authorised push payment scam: payment made to a fraudster after contact through an online marketplace and WhatsApp. ESC-1 requires Fraud & Scams, and FRD-2 requires handover within 1 business day.

open_questions: Which account was used for the transfer and what is its reference?
Exact time of the payment and the payee account details as known (name, sort code, account number)?
Has the account been secured (any card blocks or credential resets)?
Has the customer reported the scam to Action Fraud or her own bank, and is a crime reference held?
Is the marketplace listing and seller profile preserved?

analysis.suggested_next_step: Hand over to Fraud & Scams within 1 business day of 30/10/2026 (FRD-2). Record the account security check (FRD-4), obtain payee details and the payment time, and do not promise reimbursement (FRD-5).
